Here's the whole thing, all eight steps:

1. Book adult beginner lessons — weekly, 30 to 45 minutes, at a pool that runs them. If lessons aren't an option, a patient friend who swims well works too.
2. First session: shallow end, walk around, splash your face, blow bubbles. Ten minutes. The point is your body learning that water in your face is fine.
3. Learn to exhale underwater. Chest-deep, breathe in above the surface, put your face in, blow steadily out through nose and mouth, come up. Ten reps. Never hold your breath in the water.
4. Learn to float on your back. Hold the wall or a kickboard, lean back, ears in the water, belly up, arms out. Twenty to thirty seconds at a time. This is your rescue position — you can always get air here.
5. Float face down. Same idea, arms out, face in, bubbles slow. When you need air, lift your head or roll onto your back. Ten reps of five to ten seconds.
6. Glide. Push off the wall with both feet, arms stretched forward, face down, and travel without moving. Then add gentle kicks. This is where swimming actually starts.
7. Add breathing to the glide. Turn your head to the side to inhale, not up, then back down, keep kicking. Every three kicks. If you're gasping, slow down.
8. Add arms, one at a time. Reach forward, pull through the water, recover over the top. Then put it all together — that's freestyle.
